quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or very close to the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Look both ways for traffic before entering.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. These vehicles drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop at the intersection, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the intersection, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then go when the road is clear.

questions.question: Where is parking allowed?

options.text: On some large sidewalks.
Within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.
25 feet away from a crosswalk.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Parking is not allowed within 20 feet of a crosswalk, within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, or on any sidewalk. Watch for red-painted curbs and no parking signs.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to destinations.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances. They help you find places when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: When leaving a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: If you are 21 or older and driving a car, at what blood alcohol level are you considered driving under the influence?

options.text: 0.02 percent or higher.
0.04 percent or higher.
0.06 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.

questions.explanation: If you are 21 or older, driving with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered driving under the influence. You can still be arrested for DUI at lower BAC levels if you have taken other drugs.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your car is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your car off the road if you can.
Do not move your car under any circumstances.
Wait for police before moving your car.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your car out of traffic if possible. Always stay at the scene and identify yourself.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol help reduce your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Yes, it lowers blood alcohol.
Yes, it cancels out the alcohol.
No, it has no effect on blood alcohol.
Yes, it raises blood alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it has no effect on blood alcohol.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot change your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk with other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to get people's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is hard because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before you get in your car to back up, walk to the back to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Talk with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something that other road users do not expect. Talk with other drivers, cyclists, and walkers by using signals when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should slow down.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: When using a freeway exit ramp, do not slow down until you move onto the ramp.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.explanation: Regulation signs control traffic speed and movement and show rules that drivers must follow. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Side with the lightest traffic.
Same side where traffic is moving.
Side facing oncoming traffic.
Side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic in the nearest lane.

questions.question: A regulation sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers should drive under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Some regulation signs forbid certain actions. These signs are rectangular, white, with red and black markings. A red circle and slash on a black symbol means the action is not allowed.

questions.question: Traffic signals use arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A solid red arrow means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a circular red traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a circular red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red traffic light. When an arrow is red, traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: If it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes. You must do this safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: You may use your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Have lost control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to danger.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers of road work and maintenance ahead. Slow down and drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people near the road. Do not stop just to look.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a low ground railroad crossing. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, your first step should be:

options.text: Firmly apply your brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow more, gently press your brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: In Idaho, which rule applies to bicyclists?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at all stop signs.
Never ride within two feet of a right-hand curb.
Stay off all sidewalks.
Yield the right-of-way to vehicles that have already arrived at a controlled intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles that have already arrived at a controlled intersection.
questions.explanation: In Idaho, bicyclists do not need to stop at stop signs. However, they must yield to vehicles already at a stop-sign intersection and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs order drivers to follow the instruction shown. You can be penalized if you do not obey.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The maximum speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and prudent.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a reasonable and safe speed for conditions. Consider the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. Always stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you complete the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane of the street.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane of the street.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to where you started.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center of your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming straight at you, honk your horn first to get their attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Do not steer left—the other driver might correct and you'll still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Slowing down is your first step when visibility is poor or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming car has bright headlights?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is coming at you with high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This stops the light from blinding you.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately and let it pass.
Drive as far right as you safely can and stop.
Move slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly, staying on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive as far right as you safely can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is using lights or a siren, you must get out of its way. Drive to the right side of the road as far as is safe and stop. Do not stop inside an intersection.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, you should look toward which part of the road?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when a vehicle's high beams are blinding you. This keeps you from being blinded and allows you to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow at a traffic light, you:

options.text: Should move into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow tells you that you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you need to stop fast and your car does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Press down on the brake pedal hard.
Pump your brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop faster and you can still steer.

questions.question: If a solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center, what does it mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is coming up.
You will be required to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge shows where the road ends. When this line angles toward the center of the road, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about railroad crossings ahead. Use extra caution when approaching a railroad crossing.
